summary:
This app helps astronauts to monitor their health and their fitness. It also helps astronauts to monitor their nutrition.

It works like a journal entry, and the astronauts have to do the entry every day so that they can track their health. It is important because it also includes features like family messages, and it also has immersive experiences for sleep, including things like audios of places on Earth which is SI generated.

It also includes an emergency button which sends signal to the Mission Control Centre 
and also guides the astronaut on what to do.
details:
Our project, ORBITWELL, is like a journal for astronauts in space, except that it records their health, heart rate, and other important health-related information.

One of its major benefits is that it helps document changes in radiation levels. It also includes an SI model that can analyze retinal eye-scan images to identify patterns associated with eye conditions such as papilledema and pseudopapilledema.

The application also has an emergency button that sends an alert to Earth-based Mission Control. It allows the astronaut to communicate an emergency and receive an acknowledgement from Mission Control. The application also includes emergency guidance as part of its planned functionality.

We have used Python and Claude Code to develop this project. We have also used Google Teachable Machine to train an image classification model that is integrated into the application (the one for analyzing retinal eye scans).

Our project is creative because we have not only developed a dashboard for astronauts in space but also a separate dashboard for people working in Mission Control. It also focuses on the mental health of astronauts by including SI-generated relaxation audio to create calming experiences. Astronauts can also receive messages from their families, helping them stay emotionally connected to Earth.

While developing this project, our team considered the challenges of living in a simulated space environment and used them as inspiration for creating a realistic mission-support experience. We also considered how staying away from Earth and loved ones for extended periods could negatively affect astronauts' mental health.

Furthermore, eye-related conditions can occur during spaceflight, and astronauts are not necessarily trained medical professionals. Medical specialists on Earth may need to review these conditions. This is why we developed and trained an image classification model to help identify patterns associated with certain eye conditions and support further medical review.
projectRefs: How astronauts take care of their mental health in space
